transcript:
Header: Harbor Analytics - Inference Scaling & Streaming (Discovery)
Date/time: 2027-03-04 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Morales (CTO - Harbor), Priya Iyer (ML Eng Lead), Ethan Brooks (Infra)
---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros? I'm Sofia, account lead for Redwood Inference.
[00:18] Daniel: Daniel here, CTO at Harbor. We've been looking for a replacement for our in-house serving stack; latency and burst are killing us.
[00:28] Priya: Priya, leads ML infra. main goal is to serve interactive analytics chat with p95 we can commit to.
[00:38] Liam: Liam Chen, platform SE. I'll walk through how we profile and what a POC looks like.
[00:50] Ethan: Ethan, infra. i'll be focused on network, VPC and key mgmt questions.
[01:05] Sofia: Great. high-level agenda: clarify targets (p95), concurrency & token/sec needs, streaming behavior, security requirements, then agree next steps for a POC.
[01:30] Daniel: To kick off — our product is a conversational analytics UI. typical response lengths are 40-250 tokens, sometimes longer for summaries. our goal: p95 under 600ms for streaming responses at steady state, spike handling up to 400 concurrent users.
[01:58] Priya: We also need sustained throughput numbers because we'll have batch backfills and some nightly indexing — token/sec matters for cost.
[02:18] Liam: Understood. couple clarifying qs: when you say 400 concurrent users, do you mean 400 simultaneous streaming sessions or 400 concurrent requests spread across endpoints?
[02:36] Priya: Streaming sessions — they keep an open stream while tokens are emitted. in practice it's about 300-450 active streams during US peak.
[02:50] Sofia: And target p95 is for the end-to-end user-visible latency? including network, or strictly inference?
[02:58] Daniel: end-to-end user visible, yes. so we have to budget for client/network too. but inference must be predictable — our SLA needs to be meaningful.
[03:12] Liam: makes sense. rough ballpark we often see: Hosted for quick trials, Dedicated pools for predictable p95 at scale, Private if you need on-prem or strict VPC-only. each has tradeoffs on cost and isolation.
[03:34] Ethan: Our security posture likely pushes us to Dedicated or Private — we need KMS integration and audit logs, SOC2 evidence.
[03:45] Sofia: We are SOC2 + ISO mapped; we can share the pack. KMS integration and VPC peering are supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports customer keys for some tiers but we'll share specifics.
[04:05] Liam: back to latency: do you prioritize p95 at short responses (40-100 tokens) or long (200-250 tokens)? batching and KV cache behavior differ.
[04:22] Priya: Short responses are the heart of the UX. long summaries can be async. so p95 at 50-100 tokens is most important.
[04:34] Daniel: Also need to handle spikes triggered by product launches — short-lived bursts 2-3x baseline.
[04:46] Liam: ok. so design goals: steady-state p95 < 600ms for 50-100 tokens streaming, handle 2-3x bursts to 400 streams, and cost envelope.
[05:00] Sofia: Can you share current metrics? latency histograms, token/sec, burst patterns?
[05:12] Priya: We have one week of telemetry ready — i'll share histograms and sample prompts.
[05:20] (pause)
[05:40] Liam: On the technology side: we use continuous batching, KV cache, and prefix caching on some routes. for streaming we preserve token-by-token delivery but we tune batch windows to meet p95. quantization helps throughput but can change quality; we'll discuss tradeoffs.
[06:05] Daniel: how do you typically benchmark p95 for streaming? we've seen vendors report token/sec but that doesn't map to p95.
[06:20] Liam: good point. we run synthetic streaming workloads with timing that mimic your client-side RTT and emission patterns. we report both per-request p50/p95/p99 and cluster-level token/sec under specified concurrency. we also measure cold-start and warmed-cache profiles.
[06:44] Priya: what's a realistic token/sec target for us? we're expecting peaks up to 40k tokens/sec across the cluster during high activity windows.
[06:56] Liam: 40k aggregate tokens/sec is doable on Dedicated pools with the right GPU mix; we often size by tokens/sec *and* concurrent streams. rough rule: if most responses are 50 tokens and you have 400 concurrent streams, steady token/sec ~ 50 * 400 / average response interval. if responses are emitted slowly it's different.
[07:26] Daniel: can you give a sample config that meets our p95 goal?
[07:34] Liam: sure — for example, a Dedicated pool of N midsize GPUs with model variants (quantized) and a short batching window can provide shorter tail latencies. but exact numbers require our benchmark with your prompts.
[07:50] Priya: do you support autoscaling during bursts? we don't want to overpay but need headroom.
[07:58] Sofia: yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and burst capacity options. we can set a predictive autoscale with a warm-up buffer; for POC we usually enable manual burst so behavior is deterministic.
[08:15] Ethan: network — we need VPC peering and private IP egress. latency from our app to the inference endpoint must be stable. what network topologies do you support?
[08:28] Liam: Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and private endpoints. in Hosted we offer regional endpoints and TLS; some enterprise Hosted tiers support VPC access. we'll need to map your VPC and firewall rules.
[08:45] Daniel: another constraint — we must use our KMS (AWS KMS) for key wrapping. is that supported?
[08:53] Sofia: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys; Hosted has a bring-your-key option for some tiers. we'll include KMS integration doc.
[09:06] Priya: what about fallbacks — if the Dedicated pool is saturated can requests fall back to a cheaper model? we want graceful degradation.
[09:16] Liam: Redwood supports smart routing and fallbacks; you can define policies that prefer low-latency variants and fallback to cost-optimized ones when capacity is constrained. fallbacks can be regional or model-variant based.
[09:32] Daniel: and how do you guarantee the p95? do you offer any SLA?
[09:38] Sofia: Dedicated has SLA-backed latency targets at certain commitment levels. we'll share the SLA doc. for Hosted we have uptime SLAs; latency SLAs are contractual for enterprise deals.
[09:52] Priya: for the POC, we'd like to validate p95 at our traffic and see cost implications of quantization vs non-quantized models.
[09:59] Liam: plan would be: 1) run our benchmark script against a Dedicated test pool configured to mirror your workload; 2) report per-route p95, token/sec, and cost estimates; 3) iterate on batching/quantization.
[10:18] Daniel: timeline-wise, we want results within two weeks. is that realistic?
[10:25] Liam: yes — if you provide traffic histogram and sample prompts this week, we can run bench and deliver results in ~7-10 business days.
[10:36] Sofia: we'll also include pricing scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private to show TCO.
[10:44] Ethan: about observability — we need per-token cost and per-route latency breakdowns, traces to link requests back to user IDs for debugging (masked), and audit logs.
[10:59] Liam: Redwood Console supports token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and exportable logs. audit logs and retention levels are configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[11:20] Priya: any limitations with streaming long contexts? we use rolling context up to 8k tokens sometimes.
[11:30] Liam: runtime supports long context but kernel selection and memory management affect p95; for very long contexts you may see increased p95. we can use KV cache strategies to limit repeated prefix work.
[11:45] Daniel: do you support model pinning and canary rollouts?
[11:51] Sofia: yes — rollout controls, canaries and automatic fallback policies are supported so you can test new versions safely.
[12:00] (crosstalk)
[12:20] Liam: quick note on tokenization differences — different model families can produce different token counts for the same prompt; that affects token/sec accounting and batching. we'll factor that into estimates.
[12:36] Priya: what's the typical variance we should expect between p50 and p95 in streaming?
[12:44] Liam: depends, but we often see p95 1.5-3x p50 for well-configured pools. misconfigured batching windows or cold caches can push that higher.
[12:58] Daniel: can you run an experiment where you simulate our client RTT (we have 80-120ms median) and measure end-to-end user-visible p95?
[13:12] Liam: absolutely — include client RTT in the bench harness. we'll produce both inference-only and end-to-end numbers.
[13:24] Sofia: security questions — we'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts; any additional compliance we should prepare for?
[13:33] Ethan: we might need HIPAA scoped controls for a specific line of products later; for now SOC2/ISO and KMS are enough.
[13:43] Liam: Private deployment is available if you need air-gapped or on-prem later; Dedicated can bridge most enterprise needs today.
[13:56] Daniel: pricing — we need a clear cost per 1M tokens for Hosted and an hourly/reservation model for Dedicated.
[14:05] Sofia: we'll send a pricing deck with Hosted per-token tiers and Dedicated reserved capacity examples. expect a few scenarios with quantized/non-quantized variants.
[14:16] Priya: in prior vendors we saw unexpected cost spikes due to long tail retries; how do you protect against that?
[14:28] Liam: we have rate limiting, retry policies, and circuit breakers at route level plus cost dashboards; you can set soft caps and alerts.
[14:40] Daniel: for POC we'll need a non-prod test environment with similar topology. can you provision a test Dedicated pool?
[14:50] Sofia: yes — for POC we'll spin up a short-lived Dedicated test pool or a hosted test config, whichever you prefer.
[15:00] Ethan: latency to/from our infra — we'll run a quick network test to proposed endpoints.
[15:08] (brief pause)
[15:30] Priya: wanted to ask about model variants for fallback — do you keep smaller models with similar output quality?
[15:39] Liam: we maintain a catalog of verified model variants and quantization states; selecting fallback depends on acceptable quality drop. we'll provide evaluation metrics and side-by-side comparisons.
[15:58] Daniel: operationally who will own the POC on your side?
[16:05] Sofia: me for coordination and Liam for engineering/run benchmarks.
[16:10] Daniel: and on our side Priya and Ethan will run validation.
[16:18] Liam: quick technical detail — for streaming p95 measurement we instrument token emission times and measure 95th percentile across tokens emitted within an interval; that gives a realistic user-visible tail.
[16:34] Priya: ok that sounds useful. also, can you emit partial tokens for UI progressive rendering?
[16:43] Liam: yes — streaming supports partial flush and chunking frequency is configurable to balance latency and throughput.
[16:52] Daniel: any gotchas with quantization and streaming? we've seen artifacts in completions when switching precision.
[17:02] Liam: quantization can introduce small quality diffs; for deterministic evaluation we recommend running both quantized and non-quantized models on sample prompts to measure regressions. we surface those in quality reports.
[17:18] Priya: will the benchmark include cost modeling? we want to see cents per 1k tokens across scenarios.
[17:26] Sofia: yes, the benchmark report will include cost breakdowns by model variant, batch config, and projected monthly spend.
[17:38] Daniel: about SLAs again — any credits if p95 is missed?
[17:45] Sofia: SLA credits are contractually defined; we'll include the latency SLA appendix for Dedicated in the deck.
[17:55] Ethan: for audit we need retention of logs for 1 year and ability to export to our SIEM.
[18:04] Liam: supported — we can stream logs to your collectors and configure retention.
[18:14] Priya: sample test data — are there privacy rules for using our prompts in bench runs? we prefer hashed/anonymized prompts.
[18:24] Sofia: completely fine — we'll accept anonymized or synthetic prompts, and we can run inside your VPC in Dedicated/Private for extra privacy.
[18:38] Daniel: last question on ops: who manages kernel selection and infra tuning during POC?
[18:46] Liam: our SEs will propose kernel and quantization config; for Dedicated we can also open a collaborative tuning window with your infra team.
[18:56] (brief laughter)
[19:10] Sofia: wrap-up time — recap of what we agreed: POC to validate p95 < 600ms for 50-100 token streaming at ~300-400 concurrent streams; run benchmark with client RTT included; provide pricing and security docs; set up test pool.
[19:34] Daniel: yes that's correct. timeline: we'll provide telemetry and prompts by Monday, you aim to deliver bench results within 7-10 business days.
[19:48] Priya: also want the benchmark script so we can re-run internally.
[19:55] Liam: will include the harness and instructions.
[20:05] Sofia: ok next steps — i'll send the pricing deck and security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS notes) and propose POC timeslots.
[20:13] Ethan: i'll follow up about network constraints and firewall rules.
[20:20] Daniel: thanks. any final questions?
[20:27] (silence)
[20:40] Sofia: no — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with action items.
[20:48] (meeting continues with brief technical asides and scheduling)
[25:12] Liam: one more note on measurement — we'll provide p95 broken down by warm/cold cache and show how KV prefix caching affects tail.
[25:30] Priya: good. also include model tokenization differences in the report.
[25:40] Liam: noted.
[26:05] (scheduling ping)
[27:00] Sofia: proposing POC kickoff Tue 2027-03-09 9am PT, does that work?
[27:12] Daniel: yes tentative calendar hold ok.
[27:18] Priya: works for me.
[27:25] Ethan: fine.
[27:40] Sofia: great. we'll send invites.
[28:02] (small talk about background)
[30:45] Sofia: final recap and I'll list owners in the follow-up. thanks everyone.
[31:00] (meeting end)
---
Recap (auto): p95 streaming target validated as priority, Dedicated test pool recommended for predictable tails, security artifacts requested, benchmark + pricing to be delivered.
